title: Use a modular Go monolith
body: Build jacu with Go 1.26.x as one binary and one go.mod, separating concerns with internal package boundaries instead of premature services or modules.

title: Keep MCP as an adapter
body: Protocol translation belongs in internal/mcpadapter. Domain policy and capability governance must remain in the runtime or capability packages.

title: Negotiate stable MCP versions through the SDK
body: Default to MCP 2026-07-28, retain negotiated compatibility with 2025-11-25 through the official Go SDK, and do not implement Roots, Sampling, or Logging MCP.

title: Use STDIO as the default transport
body: Run jacu as a local STDIO server. Adding HTTP requires demonstrated need and a separate architectural decision record.

title: Route every tool through the runtime pipeline
body: Every tool must declare a ToolSpec and pass through decode, schema, policy, control, execute, output, and audit in that order.

title: Enforce deny by default without a generic shell
body: Reject undeclared path, command, environment, or network access. Never expose a generic shell tool; annotations and skills do not authorize execution.

title: Guarantee workspace isolation and digest gated apply
body: Perform mutations in an isolated Git worktree on its own branch, and apply only when the digest matches the human-reviewed diff.

title: Share deterministic project identity across capabilities
body: Use the shared internal/project package for canonical project roots and deterministic project IDs so inspect, mission, workspace, and later capabilities agree on identity.

title: Keep response data always present as an object
body: Capability envelopes must always include data with a concrete object schema. Empty or blocked semantics live inside a value payload instead of omitting data or making it nullable.

title: Represent verification commands as executable and argv
body: Verification commands are argv-only arrays: use a known executable plus arguments with exec.CommandContext, never a shell string or sh -c.

title: Include untracked files in review with intent to add
body: Prepare a private temporary Git index with read-tree and git add --intent-to-add -A before diffing so new files appear with full content in patch, numstat, scope audit, and digest without staging the real index.

title: Revalidate the tree after verification
body: After verification commands pass, stage once, compare the canonical staged digest to the reviewed digest, pin the validated tree and parent, commit that tree, and update HEAD by compare-and-swap.

title: Organize internal packages by boundary and capability
body: Keep MCP adaptation in internal/mcpadapter, shared governance in internal/runtime, and product behavior in vertical capability slices.

title: Reserve stdout for the MCP protocol
body: The serve command writes protocol frames only to stdout. Operational logs go to stderr and must not contain secrets or complete file contents.

title: Order capability risk from read to destructive
body: Introduce read-only behavior before write behavior and write behavior before destructive behavior, with explicit truthful risk metadata at each step.

title: Confine SDK types to the MCP boundary
body: Keep official Go SDK types and protocol details in internal/mcpadapter so protocol changes do not leak into domain rules.

title: Resolve repository paths with symlink checks
body: Fix the project root at startup, normalize with Clean and Rel, evaluate symlinks, enforce an allowlist, reject paths outside the root, and fail closed.

title: Cap tool input and output sizes
body: Apply server-side byte caps rather than relying on host truncation. Keep small output inline and move larger output to an artifact according to the capability contract.

title: Treat annotations as descriptive metadata
body: Declare annotations honestly for host UX, but enforce authorization and safety in runtime policy because clients treat annotations as untrusted.

title: Build review diffs with a temporary Git index
body: Create a private GIT_INDEX_FILE, load the base tree, apply intent-to-add, produce the review snapshot, and remove the temporary directory on success or failure without touching the real index.

title: Capture patch and numstat in one Git invocation
body: Generate the human patch and physical numstat from one diff snapshot so the digest, scope audit, paths, and counts describe the same tree.

title: Build deterministic workspace commit messages
body: Derive commit content from canonical run state and append sanitized Jacu trailers for mission, run, base, and host metadata.

title: Keep workspace status a pure reader
body: Status may detect and report a corrupted or orphaned run, but it must not persist that transition or mutate repository state; write operations such as discard or GC persist recovery state.

title: List sensitive filenames without reading their contents
body: Project inspection may report that a sensitive file exists, but must never read or expose its contents. Treat repository content as untrusted data.

title: Pointer envelope data becomes nullable
body: Using Data *T makes schema inference emit type ["null","object"]. Use Data T by value so data remains present with a concrete object schema.

title: Untrusted hostName can inject commit trailers
body: ClientInfo Name is untrusted. Newlines, controls, format characters, or unbounded Unicode can forge Jacu trailers; normalize whitespace, sanitize controls, apply a fallback, and cap the host name at 128 runes.

title: Plain git diff omits untracked files
body: A review based on plain git diff can omit a new file that a later git add -A commits. This breaks the reviewed-digest guarantee unless intent-to-add includes the file before snapshotting.

title: Verification can mutate the reviewed tree
body: A verification command can exit successfully after changing files, the index, or HEAD. Checking the digest only before verification creates a TOCTOU path to commit unreviewed content.

title: Separate patch and numstat captures can disagree
body: If patch and numstat come from separate Git calls, a mutation between calls can make the human and digest see one tree while scope paths and counts describe another.

title: Intent to add can mutate the real index
body: Calling git add --intent-to-add against the worktree index changes repository state even when file contents are not staged. Read and review paths must use a temporary GIT_INDEX_FILE.

title: Persist applied state before removing the worktree
body: Removing a worktree before saving the applied commit can leave state saying reviewed after the commit already exists. Save applied state and SHA first, then unlock and remove; cleanup failure becomes an orphan warning.

title: Git index metadata can break equivalent digests
body: Review and staged diffs may have different index hash metadata despite identical content. Canonicalize both paths with one function that removes index metadata lines before hashing while retaining all content changes.

title: Rename scope needs both physical paths
body: A rename affects both the old and new physical paths. Scope auditing that keeps only one side can hide an out-of-scope change.

title: Symlink traversal can escape the project root
body: Lexical path cleaning alone is insufficient because a repository symlink can resolve outside the project. Evaluate symlinks and reject escapes before reading.

title: Generic data schema inference may emit a boolean schema
body: A generic output registration can expose properties.data as a boolean schema instead of an object. Register each tool with its concrete output type and verify the tools/list schema.

title: Advertising Logging MCP violates the protocol contract
body: The official SDK can advertise Logging unless it is explicitly disabled. jacu must keep the logging capability absent from initialization and host smoke evidence.

title: Erick always merges with a merge commit
body: Leave the final merge to Erick and use a merge commit. Never squash the reviewed phase history.

title: Use jacu-code only as a knowledge reference
body: Keep jacu-code beside jacu as a read-only source of specifications and test scenarios. Migrate contracts and tests, never Rust implementation code.

title: Deliver one capability at a time with a gate
body: Avoid rebuilding premature TUI, bridges, routing, retrieval, or agent-team surfaces. Add one capability slice at a time only when an evaluation proves the need.

title: Require explicit human approval of the reviewed diff
body: The agent proposes, code verifies, and a human approves. Present the real digest-bound diff and stop until the human explicitly approves before apply.

title: Describe cooperative gating honestly
body: Never claim that skills or tool annotations secure native host actions. Workspace isolation is guaranteed; call gating applies only when the host routes work through jacu.

title: Recovery archives require a persisted digest
body: Accepting any non-empty regular archive lets tampered recovery authorize branch cleanup. Persist the SHA-256 of raw patch bytes before cleanup and fail closed on retry when the digest is missing or mismatched.

title: Prefer truthful destructive annotations over convenience
body: Mark apply and discard destructive when they remove worktree files, even if content is preserved elsewhere. Extra host confirmation aligns with the human gate.

title: Keep agent-facing capability text in English
body: Write summaries, warnings, next actions, validation messages, and other agent-facing capability output in English for consistent behavior across hosts.

title: Freeze jacu-code after workspace coverage is proven
body: Move jacu-code to maintenance after jacu covers inspect, mission, and digest-gated workspace apply across all five hosts in the compatibility matrix.

title: Propagate cancellation and bound active execution
body: Give each tool a timeout, propagate cancellation cleanly, avoid orphan goroutines, and permit only one active tool per process in the MVP.

title: Open world verification can access the network
body: Mission verification commands may invoke arbitrary binaries, and v1 has no kernel sandbox or network guard. Keep apply openWorldHint true until a future sandbox makes verification closed-world.

title: Transcribe regression scenarios instead of trusting memory
body: When migrating behavior from jacu-code, turn path traversal, symlink escape, unsafe command, digest mismatch, and secret-redaction scenarios into golden or fuzz tests rather than relying on remembered implementation details.
